author_reading.workflow_class: Gray pointer FIFO and cross-clock memory

rationale: The source registers the Gray encoding of successive binary increments and the destination has two stages with matching zero reset. Unlike synchronous pin lookalikes this is a real internal crossing between explicitly asynchronous clocks. No supplied internal skew/delay bound prevents bits from successive source transitions overlapping at the receiver, and startup/release evidence is incomplete. These are legitimate unresolved Gray-pointer obligations, not proof that the RTL is defective.
